proposed_relationship: Using non-aqueous electrolytes that conduct sodium ions in rechargeable batteries with earth-abundant elements could mitigate the safety issues associated with sodium metal batteries.
mechanism: The mechanism behind this proposed relationship involves the use of non-aqueous electrolytes to facilitate the reversible insertion and extraction of sodium ions between electrodes, potentially reducing or eliminating the formation of dendrites that make sodium metal batteries unsafe. By leveraging earth-abundant elements, the cost of such batteries could be significantly reduced, making them a viable alternative to existing battery technologies. The key to this mechanism is the ability of the non-aqueous electrolytes to support the necessary ion transport without the hazards associated with sodium metal.
constraint_released: The constraint of safety issues due to dendrite formation in sodium metal batteries is released by utilizing non-aqueous electrolytes and earth-abundant elements.
